set: the eight Jesus-and-John passages, in the order Berendts printed them (1906) and Thackeray listed them (1919, Note II)
status: CONTESTED — carried as reception data, never as canonical Josephus
defined_by: Berendts 1906 (EA-CORPORA-37/05); collated in #1761, The Word That Became Text v2.0, Appendix I

repaired.note: Version 1.0 of this index carried eight paraphrases from #1176/#626 Appendix II, which are the authors' stations and not the recension's passages; three of them have no witness. They are replaced by the received eight with their loci and Old Russian from the seated text. The withdrawn paraphrases are kept below and are answered in the errata on #626.

witnesses.Meshcherskii 1958: Old Russian of all seven books, Vilna Chronograph; seated EA-CORPORA-37/01 (#1760)
witnesses.Berendts 1906: the eight passages, German; seated EA-CORPORA-37/05
witnesses.Thackeray 1928: the twenty-two additions, English; seated EA-CORPORA-37/03
witnesses.Leeming & Leeming 2003: synoptic English edition (Brill); in copyright; cited not seated

outside_the_eight: Meshcherskii also prints the Magi story at the end of Book I, chapter 20 (his addition no. 5), which Berendts and Istrin left out: 'Писано есть, яко от Вифлеома ражается помазанник' (seated text, lines 3025–3026).
transmission: Popov 1866 (first notice) → Sreznevsky 1879 (Rus' chronicle language) → Berendts 1906 (translation + Vorlage thesis) → Eisler 1931 vs. Zeitlin–Feldman–Meier consensus → Pines 1971 (Syriac-corridor plausibility)
